title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 118
paragraphs: Those within the walls, however, had now come to the utmost misery — they boiled down the girths of their beds and used them for food; and when they no longer had even these, then the Persians with Artaÿctes and Oiobazos ran away and departed in the night, climbing down by the back of the wall where the place was left most unguarded by the enemy. When day came, the men of the Chersonese signaled to the Athenians from the towers about what had happened and opened the gates to them. So most of them went in pursuit, while the rest occupied the city.
